headline: A wheel in stone. A world in motion.
opening: A wheel is a useful place to begin at Konark. Look from the spokes to the figures around them, then step back far enough to see where the wheel sits in the temple’s design.
opening_kind: Original narration grounded in the photograph; not an eyewitness account.

history.heading: Built for the sun
history.text: Narasimha Deva I’s 13th-century temple takes the form of Surya’s chariot. The great structure still standing is the jagamohana, or audience hall; the principal sanctuary has lost its tower. Farther east, the dance hall stands without its roof. These are parts of a larger temple, and recognising them makes the surviving stones easier to read.

culture_heading: A poem, a legend, a stage
culture_intro: Read the story that grew around the stones, then seek the living arts that gather beside them.

surprise.heading: The wheel is only the beginning.

metrics.label: carved wheels in the chariot design

surprise.text: Musicians, dancers, fantastic lions and erotic groups share the reliefs along the plinth. The twenty-four wheels belong to the chariot design; the figures between them invite a closer look at the lives and bodies represented in the stone.
surprise.reveal: Choose one carved figure and describe its posture before asking a guide about it. Compare what you can see with the interpretation you hear.

belief.label: Local legend · a literary retelling
belief.heading: The boy who completed the temple
belief.text: In the legend, Dharmapada, the young son of craftsman Bisu Moharana, completes the temple’s unfinished work. His success threatens the standing of the adult craftsmen, and the story ends with his death. Gopabandhu Das gave the boy’s sacrifice a literary life in his poem Dharmapada.
belief.qualification: This is a legend, not a record of the temple’s construction. Writing about Gopabandhu’s use of the story, Snigdha Acharya connects the poem with the awakening of patriotic feeling in Odisha.

invitation.heading: Choose one detail to carry home
invitation.text: A carved spoke, a dancer’s gesture, a line of shadow. Which small detail would you draw on a postcard?
invitation.kind: Editorial observation prompt; no answer collection.
